Lessons.Title: Solve Problems with Many Operations
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use the four operations to solve problems involving multi-digit numbers.
In the preceding lessons, you interpret situations and solve them using a variety of reasoning strategies. The computations focus mostly on multiplication and division, and the numbers are mainly two and three digits long. In this lesson, you continue to engage in problem solving—this time in the context of finding distances.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: True or False: Differences (10 minutes); Activity 1: Back and Forth (20 minutes); Activity 2: Fitness Challenge (15 minutes); Cool-down: Long-distance Driving (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: Use the four operations and inverse checks, preserving place value in multi-digit written methods.
Edulytics authored model: 50,000 − 999 = 50,000 − 1,000 + 1 = 49,001. 5,000 − 311 = 4,689, so 4,799 = 5,000 − 311 is false. Check each computed answer for reasonable size.
First-party Cool-down: Find 12,500 − 9,876, then check by addition.
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
